newsitem.title: USA: Court refuses to dismiss Denver airport lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Court refuses to dismiss Denver airport lawsuit.

text.p: A federal appeals court will allow a lawsuit to proceed against the city and county of Denver that alleged the city made false and misleading statements when selling Denver International Airport bonds.
Four class-action lawsuits were brought by bondholders against Denver and its underwriters.
The city sought to have the lawsuit dismissed, but a trial court judge refused its motion and the appeals court on Tuesday upheld that decision.
The United States Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit said Denver could not have the suit dismissed on the grounds that private parties cannot sue municipalities under the Securities Exchange Act.
The appeals court also rejected Denver's argument that it was immune from the lawsuit under the Eleventh Amendment to the U.S. Constitution, which limits lawsuits against U.S. states.

Also sued by the bondholders were underwriting firms, Lazard Freres; Pryor, McClendon, Counts & Co; Goldman, Sachs & Co; LS Financial Inc; Dain Bosworth Inc; Lehman Brothers Inc; Artemis Capital Group Inc and Paper Jaffray Inc.
